blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Text-to-image diffusion models can learn and reproduce an individual's identity from only a few reference photos, creating risks of unauthorized and misleading content generation. Proactive defenses address this risk by adding adversarial perturbations to facial images before release, thereby disrupting identity acquisition during downstream personalization. However, existing methods typically rely on dense $L_\infty$-bounded perturbations, whose accumulated distortions can become visible around facial structures. Recent methods improve protected-image quality, but often at the cost of reduced protection effectiveness. In this paper, we propose Sparse Encoder Attack on Latent Variance (SEAL), a sparse adversarial protection framework that modifies only 5% of the spatial locations in a facial image. SEAL combines a differentiable top-k masking scheme that jointly optimizes perturbation locations and values with a variance-oriented objective over the frozen VAE encoder's latent distribution to disrupt identity-consistent representations. A saliency-guided dispersion penalty further discourages perturbation concentration in perceptually salient facial regions. Experiments on CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2 show that SEAL achieves the best protected-image quality among the compared methods, exceeding 41 dB PSNR with 0.97 SSIM and at most 0.07 LPIPS, while reducing identity similarity to at most 0.15 after diffusion personalization. These results demonstrate that sparse location optimization enables strong identity protection while preserving high visual quality. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Lvxan/SEAL

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Text-to-image diffusion models [ 9 , 23 ] have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in generating photorealistic images from natural language descriptions.
Personalization techniques, such as DreamBooth [ 24 ] and Textual Inversion [ 6 ] , further enable these models to reproduce a specific individual from only a few reference photos.
While this capability facilitates customized content creation, it also lowers the barrier to unauthorized identity replication.
An adversary can collect publicly available facial images, personalize a diffusion model to the depicted individual, and generate misleading or harmful content involving that person [ 22 ] .
This risk motivates proactive protection mechanisms that prevent released facial images from being used to learn and reproduce an individual’s identity.
blocks.zh:
文本到图像的传播模型[9,23]在从自然语言描述中生成光现实化图像方面表现出显著的能力.
个性化技术,如DreamBooth [24] 和Textual Inversion [6] 进一步使这些模型能够从仅几张参考照片中复制特定个人.
虽然这一能力有助于定制内容的创建,但也降低了未经授权复制身份的障碍。
对手可以收集公开的面部图像,将传播模型个性化给被描绘的个人,并产生涉及该人的误导或有害内容[22].
这种风险促使人们建立积极的保护机制,防止释放的面部图像被用来学习和复制个人的身份。

blocks.en:
A common proactive strategy is to add bounded adversarial perturbations to facial images before their release, such that personalized models fine-tuned on these protected images fail to reproduce the target identity.
Early approaches construct such perturbations by maximizing the diffusion denoising loss, as in AdvDM [ 17 ] , or by shifting image representations toward a predefined latent target, as in Mist [ 16 ] .
Anti-DreamBooth [ 28 ] instead directly maximizes the DreamBooth training loss to interfere with personalization.
More recent methods, including PID [ 15 ] and Variance as a Catalyst [ 32 ] , manipulate the mean or variance of the VAE encoder’s latent distribution, revealing that disrupting latent statistics can effectively impair identity acquisition across different prompts.
Collectively, these studies establish adversarial perturbation as a viable defense against unauthorized diffusion personalization.
blocks.zh:
一个共同的主动策略是,在面部图像发布前添加有约束的对抗性扰动,这样在这些受保护图像上细化的个性化模型无法复制目标身份.
如AdvDM[17], 或如Mist[16], 将图像表达方式转向预先界定的潜在目标, 从而形成这种扰动。
Anti-DreamBooth [28] 相反,直接将DreamBooth训练损失最大化,以干扰个性化.
更近的方法,包括PID[15]和作为催化剂的差异[32],操纵VAE编码器潜在分布的平均值或差异,揭示干扰潜在统计会有效地妨碍不同提示获得身份。
这些研究共同确立了对抗性扰动作为防止未经授权扩散个人化的可行辩护.

blocks.en:
However, most existing methods apply dense perturbations across every pixel, and the accumulated distortions can become perceptible around visually sensitive facial structures.
Recent works have sought to improve perceptual quality: VCPro [ 20 ] uses concept masks to guide a regional adversarial objective, whereas MYOPIA [ 30 ] exploits local information to conceal perturbation artifacts. However, these improvements in visual quality are accompanied by reduced protection effectiveness.
Overall, existing methods exhibit a pronounced trade-off between protection and visual quality. As shown in Figure 1 , methods that achieve stronger protection often rely on dense perturbations that noticeably degrade image quality, whereas visual-friendly methods preserve quality at the cost of reduced protection effectiveness. Achieving strong protection while maintaining high visual quality therefore remains an open challenge.
blocks.zh:
然而,大多数现有方法在每一个像素中都应用了密集的扰动,累积的扭曲现象可以在视觉敏感的面部结构周围被察觉到.
近期的作品力求提高知觉质量:VCPro[20]使用概念口罩指导区域对抗目标,而MYOPIA[30]则利用当地信息隐藏扰动文物. 然而,在视觉质量的这些改善的同时,保护的有效性也有所下降。
总体而言,现有方法显示出保护与视觉质量之间的明显权衡。 如图1所示,加强保护的方法往往依赖密集的扰动,这种扰动明显降低图像质量,而方便视觉的方法则以降低保护效力为代价来保持质量。 因此,在保持高视力的同时实现强有力的保护仍然是一个公开的挑战。

blocks.en:
To address this challenge, we propose S parse E ncoder A ttack on L atent Variance ( SEAL ), a sparse perturbation framework for proactive face privacy protection.
Instead of distributing perturbations densely across the entire image, SEAL jointly optimizes a bounded perturbation δ \delta and a binary mask m m that determines the perturbed pixel locations.
To handle the discrete pixel-selection process, we adapt the differentiable top- k k masking mechanism of Sparse-PGD [ 36 ] , which jointly optimizes perturbation values and spatial locations under a fixed support budget.
Within the selected sparse support, SEAL maximizes a Laplace objective over the variance of the VAE encoder distribution, following prior evidence that disrupting latent statistics can interfere with the acquisition of subject-specific identity information [ 15 , 32 ] .
However, sparse optimization may concentrate perturbations around salient facial structures, making local artifacts noticeable even when the overall perturbation support is small.
We therefore introduce a saliency-guided dispersion regularizer that penalizes high local perturbation density in perceptually salient facial regions.
Together, these components allow SEAL to allocate a limited perturbation budget to locations that effectively disrupt personalization while preserving the visual quality of the protected image.

This improvement is mainly due to the way the locations of the perturbations are placed.
Ablation experiments show that when the 5% locations are chosen at random rather than optimized, ISM rises from 0.07 to 0.68.
Qualitatively, as shown in Figure 3 , the protected images preserve high visual quality in facial-detail regions, while DreamBooth generations under different prompts are severely disrupted.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Personalized Text-to-Image Generation
blocks.zh: 2.1 个性化文本对图像生成

blocks.en:
Text-to-image diffusion models have become a dominant paradigm for image synthesis, with latent diffusion models [ 23 ] improving computational efficiency by performing denoising in a compressed latent space. Beyond generic generation, personalization techniques adapt pretrained diffusion models to reproduce a specific subject or visual concept from only a few reference images. Textual Inversion [ 6 ] learns a new token embedding to represent the target visual concept, whereas DreamBooth [ 24 ] fine-tunes the generative model to bind a unique identifier to the target subject. Custom Diffusion [ 13 ] enables multi-concept customization, and LoRA [ 10 ] reduces fine-tuning cost.
When applied to human faces, however, such personalization capabilities raise serious privacy and security concerns, as publicly available photographs can be exploited to generate misleading or unauthorized depictions of specific individuals [ 22 ] .

blocks.en: 2.2 Image Protection Against Personalization
blocks.zh: 2.2 防止个人化的图像保护

blocks.en:
To mitigate unauthorized personalization, most protection methods add adversarial perturbations to images before release to disrupt their use in downstream diffusion personalization, though a separate line instead pursues privacy on the model side by training identity-decoupled personalized models [ 2 ] .
These input-side methods differ primarily in the model component or training objective targeted during perturbation optimization.
AdvDM [ 17 ] maximizes the diffusion denoising loss, while PhotoGuard [ 25 ] introduces an encoder attack that shifts the latent representation toward a predefined target.
Mist [ 16 ] combines denoising and latent-target objectives to disrupt both the image representation and the denoising process.
Other methods manipulate the latent distribution produced by the VAE encoder: PID [ 15 ] jointly perturbs its mean and log-variance, whereas Variance as a Catalyst [ 32 ] develops distribution-oriented objectives, including a Laplace-based loss, to amplify latent variance and disrupt identity acquisition.
Personalization-aware methods instead incorporate the downstream training process into perturbation optimization.
Anti-DreamBooth [ 28 ] simulates DreamBooth fine-tuning and maximizes its training loss, while MetaCloak [ 18 ] employs meta-learning and transformation-aware optimization to improve perturbation transferability and robustness.
Several recent works further focus on the visual quality of protected images.
SDS(-) [ 31 ] minimizes the semantic loss to produce more natural-looking perturbations.
MYOPIA [ 30 ] combines just-noticeable-difference constraints with expectation over transformations to regulate perturbation location and intensity while improving robustness.
Latent Diffusion Unlearning [ 4 ] constructs
trajectory-shifted perturbations in latent space by alternating denoising and inversion, thereby improving the visual quality of protected images.
VCPro [ 20 ] employs selective adversarial perturbations and a relaxed optimization objective to improve the trade-off between perturbation visibility and concept protection.
Despite these advances, these methods treat perturbation placement as a visual or region-level constraint, leaving pixel-level support selection outside the optimization objective that governs protection effectiveness.
Sparse L 0 L_{0} -constrained attacks such as Sparse-PGD [ 36 ] show that adversarial effects can be achieved by modifying only a small subset of pixels.
Building on this sparse optimization principle, SEAL combines differentiable pixel selection with latent-variance disruption and saliency-guided dispersion regularization for proactive face identity protection.

blocks.en:
The attacker collects publicly available facial images of a target individual and fine-tunes a diffusion model on them with a personalization algorithm such as DreamBooth [ 24 ] , whose customized prompt binds a unique identifier such as “sks” to the subject.
The personalized model is then queried to render that individual under arbitrary prompts and contexts.

然后对个性化模式提出质询,使此人处于任意的动机和背景之下。

blocks.en:
The defender may modify images only before release and has no control over their subsequent collection or use.
The defender also has no access to the attacker’s model, personalization algorithm, training hyperparameters, identifier token, or inference prompts, and must therefore construct the protection on an accessible surrogate model.

blocks.en: 3.5 Saliency-Guided Dispersion
blocks.zh: 3.5 显著分布

blocks.en:
The sparse mask learned in Sec. 3.4 tends to concentrate perturbations in regions that yield strong latent disruption.
For facial images, these regions may coincide with perceptually sensitive structures, such as the eyes, nose, and mouth, making local perturbation artifacts more conspicuous.
To counteract this effect, we introduce a saliency-guided dispersion penalty that discourages high local perturbation density in salient facial regions.

为了抵消这种影响,我们采用了一种有突出指导的散射法,在显著面部区域抑制高局部扰动密度。

blocks.en:
We parse x x using a BiSeNet-based face parser [ 34 ] with the 19-class CelebAMask-HQ taxonomy [ 14 ] .
Studies of face viewing show that gaze is primarily allocated to internal facial features, particularly the eyes, nose, and mouth, with the eyes playing a preferential role in guiding fixations and face identification [ 8 , 7 ] .
Based on these findings, we construct the saliency map S ⁡ ( x ) S(x) by assigning each semantic class a fixed weight w c ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] w_{c}\in[0,1] , where larger values impose stronger dispersion penalties on perceptually salient regions: 1.0 1.0 for the eyes, 0.9 0.9 for the nose and mouth, 0.8 0.8 for the skin, 0.02 0.02 for the hair, and 0.0 0.0 for the background.
The weighted label map is Gaussian-smoothed and min-max normalized to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] to reduce boundary artifacts, with the complete class-to-weight mapping reported in Table 5 in the Appendix.

blocks.en: 4.1 Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 设置

blocks.en:
We evaluate SEAL on VGGFace2 [ 1 ] and CelebA-HQ [ 11 ] .
Following Anti-DreamBooth [ 28 ] , we select 50 identities from each dataset, using 4 images per identity as the target set to be protected.
Ablation studies and additional experiments use a 10-identity subset to reduce computational cost.
All images are resized to 512 × 512 512\times 512 for both perturbation generation and model fine-tuning.

我们评价海豹突击队在VGGFace2 [1]和CelebA-HQ [11].

校准研究和额外实验使用一个10个识别子集来降低计算成本.
所有图像的大小调整为512×512 512\时,既用于扰动生成,也用于模型微调.

blocks.en:
We compare against five representative protection methods:
Anti-DreamBooth [ 28 ] (Anti-DB), Mist [ 16 ] , SDS(-) [ 31 ] , MYOPIA [ 30 ] , and VCPro [ 20 ] .
These baselines cover both established protection methods and recent quality-aware approaches.
For a fair comparison, we set ϵ = 0.05 \epsilon=0.05 for all methods except MYOPIA, whose original upper bound ( ϵ = 0.5 \epsilon=0.5 ) is retained because its internal magnitude control prevents the realized perturbation from saturating this nominal budget.

For protection effectiveness, we assess the identity fidelity and perceptual quality of DreamBooth-generated images using four metrics:
ISM is the ArcFace [ 3 ] identity similarity between generated and reference facial images, FDFR is the fraction of generated images for which no face is detected, SER-FIQ [ 27 ] measures generated-face quality, and BRISQUE [ 21 ] measures no-reference image quality.

blocks.en: 4.2 Main Results

blocks.en:
Table 1 compares all methods on VGGFace2 and CelebA-HQ under two inference prompts.
With only 5% of pixels modified, SEAL achieves the best protected-image quality across all four metrics on both datasets.
Under P1, SEAL attains FDFR = = 0.93 and ISM ≤ \leq 0.11, indicating a high face-detection failure rate and low target-identity similarity.
However, baselines face a pronounced trade-off: methods with dense perturbations introduce substantial artifacts, while those preserving image quality provide negligible identity disruption.
Under prompt P2, SEAL achieves the lowest ISM on both datasets ( ≤ \leq 0.15), indicating the lowest target-identity fidelity among the compared methods.
Extended results under other prompts are reported in Appendix C.4 .

Our protected images are nearly indistinguishable from the originals: the sparse perturbation leaves 95% of pixels untouched, and the saliency-guided dispersion penalty prevents visible clustering on facial regions.
Baselines, by contrast, introduce noticeable texture distortions or color shifts.

blocks.en:
Table 4 reports the results.
Replacing the learned top- k k mask with a random mask degrades ISM from 0.07 to 0.68, showing that learned mask placement is critical under a sparse budget.
The Laplace-based (LA) loss achieves ISM 0.07, outperforming the mean-squared-error (MSE) loss at 0.37 and the Lagrange Entropy (LE) loss [ 32 ] at 0.25; both alternative objectives are defined in Appendix C.1 .
Removing the saliency penalty improves protection, reducing ISM to 0.02, while leaving global LPIPS nearly unchanged.
Since global LPIPS can obscure local distortion, we additionally report F-LPIPS: a facial mask is obtained by applying SAM [ 12 ] to the clean image and then applied to the protected image to compute mean LPIPS within the facial region.
The lower F-LPIPS of the full model shows that the saliency term reduces facial distortion by dispersing perturbations away from salient regions, at a modest cost in protection strength.
As Figure 5 shows, the mask without the dispersion penalty concentrates around the eyes and nose, while the full model distributes the selected locations more broadly across less salient regions.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we propose SEAL , an L 0 L_{0} -constrained sparse perturbation framework for face privacy protection. SEAL modifies only a small fraction of pixels and targets the VAE encoder’s latent variance to achieve strong identity disruption under a tight perturbation budget.
A saliency-guided dispersion penalty further suppresses perceptible concentration in perceptually salient facial regions.
Comprehensive experiments on CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2 demonstrate that, with only 5% of pixels perturbed, SEAL attains the best protected-image quality and the lowest identity similarity among the compared baselines.
By optimizing where the sparse perturbation lands, SEAL achieves strong protection and high image quality together.
blocks.zh:
我们提议海豹突击队, 海豹突击队只修改了一小部分像素,并瞄准了VAE编码器的潜在差异,以便在紧张的扰动预算下实现强大的身份干扰.
显性导散罚进一步抑制了在显性显性面部区域的可见浓度.
CelebA-HQ和VGGFace2的综合实验表明,由于只有5%的像素受到干扰,海豹突击队在比较基线中达到最佳保护图像质量和最低身份相似性。
海豹突击队通过优化零星的扰动地段,共同实现强大的保护和高图像质量.

blocks.en:
SEAL targets fine-tuning-based personalization, in which the protected images pass through the VAE encoder during training.
Like other protections that target the VAE encoder, it does not affect encoder-based personalization methods such as IP-Adapter FaceID [ 33 ] .
Smoothing pre-processing, such as JPEG compression, Gaussian blur, and resizing, removes most of the sparse perturbation and largely restores identity similarity (Table 8 in the appendix), whereas mild additive noise is tolerated.
This vulnerability is shared by pixel-level protective perturbations in general [ 26 ] , and improving robustness to such transformations is left for future work.
blocks.zh:
海豹突击队的目标是基于微调的个性化,其中受保护的图像在训练期间通过VAE编码器.
与其他针对VAE编码器的保护一样,它不影响IP-Adapter FaceID等基于编码器的个性化方法[33].
平滑的预处理,如JPEG压缩,高斯模糊,以及再大小化,可以去除大部分稀疏的扰动,并基本恢复身份相似性(附录表8),而轻度添加噪音则被容忍.
这种脆弱性与像素级保护性扰动具有共同性[26],改进这种转变的稳健性留待今后的工作。

blocks.en:
We conduct experiments on two widely used face datasets, CelebA-HQ [ 11 ] and VGGFace2 [ 1 ] , following prior privacy-protection work [ 28 , 20 ] .
CelebA-HQ is a high-quality version of CelebA consisting of 30,000 celebrity face images, while VGGFace2 is a large-scale dataset with over 3.3 million images from 9,131 identities.
From each dataset we select 50 identities for the main comparison and 10 identities for additional experiments; for each identity we use 4 images as the target set to be protected and reserve an additional set of clean images as identity references for evaluation.

blocks.en: B.5 Evaluation Metrics
blocks.zh: B.5 评价计量

blocks.en: We report metrics along two dimensions: the image quality of the protected image and the protection effectiveness against personalized generation.
blocks.zh: 我们从两个方面报告衡量标准:受保护图像的图像质量和针对个人化一代的保护效力。

blocks.en:
Image quality measures the distortion between a protected image and its clean counterpart.
PSNR and SSIM [ 29 ] quantify pixel- and structure-level fidelity (higher is better), whereas LPIPS [ 35 ] and DISTS [ 5 ] measure deep perceptual and structure–texture distance (lower is better).
blocks.zh:
图像质量测量受保护的图像与干净的对应图像之间的扭曲.
PSNR 和 SSIM [29] 量化像素和结构级的忠诚度(更高更好),而LPIPS [35] 和 DISTS [5] 测量深度感知和结构-纹理距离(较低更好).

blocks.en:
Protection effectiveness evaluates the DreamBooth-generated images in terms of identity and perceptual quality.
ISM (Identity Score Metric) is the ArcFace [ 3 ] cosine similarity between generated and reference faces; a lower value means less of the target identity is reproduced.
FDFR (Face Detection Failure Rate) is the fraction of generated images in which a face detector fails to locate any face; a higher value indicates stronger protection.
SER-FIQ [ 27 ] is a no-reference face image quality score, for which a lower value reflects less recognizable generated faces.
BRISQUE [ 21 ] is a no-reference image quality metric, for which higher values indicate more artifacts in the generated images.
blocks.zh:
保护效果从身份和知觉质量的角度评价DreamBooth生成的图像.
ISM(IDentity Score Metric)是生成面和参考面相的ArcFace [3] 余弦相似性;一个较低的值表示复制的目标身份较少.
FDFR(Face Second Unfail rate)是生成的图像中一个面部探测器无法定位任何面部的一小部分;更高的值表示保护性更强.
SER-FIQ [27] 是一个无参考面部图像质量分数,对此,较低的值反映了不太能识别的生成面部.
BRISQUE [21] 是一个无参考图像质量的度量标准,其较高的值表示生成的图像中有更多的文物.

Complementing the quantitative transfer results in the main text (Fig. 4 ), Fig. 8 shows qualitative generations when the protected images, optimized on the SD 2.1 surrogate, are used to personalize unseen backbones and methods.

We evaluate common image pre-processing that an adversary or platform might apply before fine-tuning.
Table 8 reports results on VGGFace2 under JPEG compression, Gaussian blur, additive Gaussian noise, downsampling round-trip, and center crop-resize, for both our default setting and the denser λ = 0 \lambda{=}0 variant.
Additive noise, which does not selectively erase the sparse perturbation, is tolerated well (default ISM = 0.13 =0.13 at σ = 2 \sigma{=}2 ), whereas smoothing transforms (JPEG, blur, resize) remove part of the localized signal.
The λ = 0 \lambda{=}0 variant attains stronger raw protection (no transform: ISM 0.00 0.00 vs. 0.09 0.09 ) and slightly better noise tolerance, but under smoothing transforms both settings converge, reflecting a general trade-off between imperceptibility and robustness rather than an effect specific to λ \lambda .
This degradation under smoothing is consistent with prior findings that pixel-level protective perturbations are broadly vulnerable to real-world image transformations [ 26 ] , and improving such robustness remains an open direction.

添加噪音不会有选择地抹去稀疏的扰动,但得到很好的容忍(默认ISM=0.13=0.13 at ç = 2\sigma{=}2),而平滑变换(JPEG,模糊,大小调整)则去除局部信号的一部分.
QQ = 0\lambda{=}0 变体实现更强的原始保护(没有变体:ISM 0.00 0.00 vs. 0.09)和稍好一些的噪声耐受性,但在平滑变体下,两种设置都趋同,反映了不易感和强力之间的普遍权衡,而不是Q&lambda特有的效果.
平滑下的这种降解与先前的调查结果是一致的,即像素级的保护扰动在总体上容易发生现实世界的图像变换[26],改善这种稳健性仍然是一个开放的方向.
